lead_notes: Four wave-1 branches were merged before any of them was gated, and 6d496b8c's conformance failures then made cargo-ci red on main for every issue at once, blocking completion of five otherwise-finished issues. The protocol 3019eacd rewrote names exactly this: gate after each merge whenever per-merge attribution matters. Gate before merging the next branch from here on.

A backgrounded `codex exec` blocks forever on 'Reading additional input from stdin...' unless stdin is redirected from /dev/null. The 6d496b8c rework sat 17 minutes with a live process, a clean worktree, no commits and 00:00:00 CPU before this was found. It is a harness defect, not a worker failure, and does not count against the rework budget.

Session 2 resumed after session 1 ended mid-run. Session 1 left four issues merged on main with a failing code-review gate (06f1fa95, 3923fd06, 89a7e34e, 57675b68), one issue fully gated but not transitioned (76a4bd21), and one worker's uncommitted design in its worktree (57675b68, preserved as 0f0fb836 on worktree-agent-57675b68).

The lead pushed main to origin at b4859c87 to start a hosted CI run. REQ-08 can only be evidenced by a completed hosted run, and a run costs wall-clock the container does not control, so it starts as early as the tree allows rather than at completion.

TRAP: a seeded regression reached main, through two faults that combined. The worker's REQ-04 re-verification ran in the parent checkout rather than its worktree — a `run_in_background` Bash call resets the session cwd, and every following command inherited the parent silently without a `cd` to reveal it. Its `sed -i` seed therefore landed on main. The lead then ran `git add -A` on main without reading `git status`, which committed the seed; the worker's `git checkout -- <path>` a moment later restored the file to that just-committed seeded state, and its `git diff --quiet` read clean because HEAD had moved under it. Neither fault alone would have shipped it: the revert would have worked, or there would have been nothing to sweep. Three habits follow — prefix every worker command with its worktree path rather than relying on session cwd; never `git add -A` on main unread while a worker is alive; and verify a revert against a known-good expected line rather than against `git diff --quiet`, which only says the tree matches HEAD and not that HEAD is right.

Workers run plain `cargo` commands, which do not take the host build lock that `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` re-execs under — only concurrent cargo-ci runs queue. Two live workers therefore starved a lead gate run to its 900-second runner timeout. Gate on main only when no worker is building.

BLOCKER at the end of wave 4: 63 orphaned busy-wait processes from 15afa1f8's load experiment saturate the host, and the lead's shell cannot signal them — the kill reports success while the processes survive, and the harness refuses the pattern-matching form as a self-match hazard. They are spin loops the worker spawned to saturate the host for a 20-repetition experiment; their parent shell died before its cleanup ran, so init adopted them. They are niced, and scripts/cargo-ci.sh also runs niced, so the gate competed with them on equal footing and overran its 900-second runner budget. The operator clears them by selecting processes whose parent is init, whose command line names the agent-15afa1f8 worktree and contains the spin loop, and killing that pid list.

Session 3 resumed with one child open and a code-review failure uncommitted. Two lessons. First, an adversarial reviewer will re-find an owner-approved mechanism under a later issue's criteria: the same thirty-second bound failed once under 57675b68 and again under 4c700c80, because 4c700c80's criteria were written before the mechanism was shared. When a container amends a criterion to permit a mechanism, sweep every sibling criterion that names the same subject in the same amendment. Second, the survey that closed REQ-05 contradicted itself — its Result claimed no flippable assertion while its own retained table recorded one — and the reviewer found the contradiction rather than the code. A document that both states a claim and tabulates its exceptions must have the claim read against the table before it is submitted.

The owner's two mid-session questions did more for the container than the third review round did. Asked whether any test could wait thirty seconds for nothing, the answer was yes and no reviewer had named it; asked for the suite to be fast, the fix that followed cut two seeded failures from 30.00 s to 0.00 s. A lead that has just won a criteria amendment should ask what the mechanism actually costs before treating the argument as settled.

Decided by the lead rather than re-escalated: an unbounded retry is not acceptable. REQ-08 exists because one unbounded wait in this suite held four CI jobs to a six-hour ceiling, so reintroducing one into the same gate is the failure mode the container closes. The bound must not be a wall clock the caller races; the preserved session-1 design bounds on claimant progress and fails loudly on a stuck lock, and the rework worker was told to adopt, improve or replace it against that decision.

Owner amended REQ-01. The reviewer failed the 30-second progress bound as a wall clock, and removing it restores the unbounded wait REQ-08 exists to close. REQ-01 now permits a bound that fires only when no claimant at all has been answered and fails loudly; the code is unchanged and the survey records the bound as retained with its exposure stated.

escalations.topic: 4c700c80's REQ-01 and REQ-05 versus the shared stall bound
escalations.resolution: Owner amended both. code-review failed the thirty-second CONTENTION_STALL_LIMIT: where one contender waits alone the set stops moving after its first refusal, so the bound runs against the holder being scheduled to release. Removing it restores the unbounded wait the container's REQ-08 exists to close, which is the trade the owner already ruled on for 57675b68's REQ-01. REQ-01 now permits a bound that fires only when nothing the wait watches has progressed and fails loudly naming what it last saw; REQ-05 now asks the survey to report every remaining flippable assertion with the argument for its retention rather than to report their absence. Code unchanged apart from a doc comment that had claimed a healthy run never spends the bound.
Owner approved the amendment raised in session 2. Applied in session 3.

The lesson is recorded in lead_notes: amend every sibling criterion naming the mechanism's subject in the same change.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: scripts/assemble-package-selftest.sh passes and covers every criterion, but nothing runs it: no gate, no CI job, and no Rust test invokes it, so the argument contract can regress without any check failing. The repository has both patterns — workflow-contract-selftest.sh runs from a CI step and verify-commit-builds-selftest.sh from a Rust test in crates/jit/tests/scratch_build, while install-jit-selftest.sh, benchmark-session-cost-selftest.sh and generate-shipped-policy-regions-selftest.sh are unwired.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Closed. The code-review gate independently raised it as blocking, citing the container's REQ-06. 3019eacd kept crates/jit/tests/scratch_build and put merged_tree_gate_verification_tests.rs there to run cargo-ci-selftest.sh from a Rust test, so the wiring precedent was alive rather than about to disappear. Fixed lead-direct at 7e1df315 by adding a module to that same suite; verified passing.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The merged change failed cargo-ci on main: adding a command surface requires registering it in every conformance suite that enumerates command surfaces, and four were missed — the classifier table in crates/jit/src/main.rs (repaired lead-direct), the row-set equality guard and both end-to-end subprocess bindings in command_exit_code_projection_tests, and the clap-arm probe in failure_probe_coverage_tests.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The teardown's drained assertion reads an unreaped zombie as a surviving process, so on a host whose PID 1 never reaps orphans the case could fail spuriously after its 15-second teardown budget. The worker judged the risk low on a virtual-machine runner and kept the strict check because it is the direct evidence for REQ-02.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted. The failure mode is a bounded failure rather than the unbounded hang the issue exists to remove, and the message distinguishes a live survivor from a zombie by reporting whether the announced port still answers.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The test's kill_process_group calls the same nix primitive under the same pid-safety guard as the private helper at crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs:345, rather than sharing it. The worker named this against @/inv/convention-convergence rather than leaving it silent.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted. The product helper is private to its module and takes a Child, so an integration test cannot reach it; exporting production API for a test's use is the worse trade. The shared mechanism actually at stake — the guarded conversion that keeps a negation from becoming kill(-1) — is followed and cited.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: setup_repo now bounds and captures its jit init, which widens the change to all ten tests in the module rather than the foreground case alone.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted. REQ-03 says every wait the test performs is bounded, and the foreground case's own setup is one of those waits; a second parallel setup helper would have violated @/inv/convention-convergence. All ten tests pass.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: code-review found read_capture's fs::read_to_string bounded by no deadline, citing the container's REQ-08, while the issue's own REQ-03 says every wait, read and join is bounded.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Reworked. A regular-file read terminates at EOF so it cannot hang like a pipe, and that argument is why the code looked correct — but the criterion says reads are bounded and this one was not. The worker chose a byte cap over a deadline and explained why the deadline is the illusion: nothing cancels a read already issued, so a deadline bounds the observer while the read runs on.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The worker reported auditing all 1545 REQ occurrences and finding every one sound. The claim does not survive as stated: plain `git log` ownership makes the test-consolidation issue 8d4f7084 a phantom owner of every file it moved, which flags roughly 29 files spuriously, and the report drew no line between attribution comments and synthetic fixture data.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Conclusion upheld, evidence rebuilt by the lead. With `git log --follow` ownership and fixtures separated from attributions, five bare occurrences remain and all five are synthetic. The commit body carries the method rather than the assertion.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: A cargo-ci evaluation hit the gate's own 900-second runner timeout and recorded status `error` rather than a verdict. The same gate over the same tree took 421 s idle and 537 s under a deliberate load test earlier in this session; this run coincided with two workers each running `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test`, carrying the host to a load average of 116 on 24 cores.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Not a REQ-03 violation, and not fixed by widening the timeout. The gate refused to answer rather than answering differently: `error` is distinguishable from `pass` and `fail`, and no verdict was produced from a starved run. Raising the 900-second budget would be a margin chosen to be long enough, which is the defect class this container exists to remove. The operational remedy is scheduling: the lead does not evaluate cargo-ci while a worker is building. Recorded because the observation is real and a reader comparing run durations will otherwise wonder.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The worker's load experiment spawned 64 busy-wait spinners to saturate the host, ran the test 20 times against them, and was to kill them afterwards. Its parent shell died before the cleanup ran, orphaning all 64 to init, where they kept burning CPU for over half an hour and starved the lead's gate run to its runner timeout.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Closed. The operator reaped them between sessions; session 3 found no process whose parent is init naming the agent-15afa1f8 worktree, and a host load average of 0.08. The dispatch rule the finding implies stands: a worker that spawns load traps its cleanup, and the lead checks for orphaned load before attributing a slow gate to anything else.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: holistic-review F2: the load-independence report stated the host load each run met as two hand-read numbers. The gate records substantiated verdicts, durations and an equal inputs digest, but nothing in the repository held the load condition itself.

The comparison was run again over one frozen tree with /proc/loadavg sampled every five seconds into load-trace-2026-08-05.csv, written outside the repository so dev/ staying constant kept the two digests equal. Gate alone 387 s at load 4.48-24.36; under nine concurrent workspace rebuilds and a 12-way CPU load 522 s at 18.70-57.91 on 24 cores. Both passed, both digest 1b6acff4.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The trace's first phase is labelled idle, and it is not: the gate's own compilation and test parallelism carries the host to a 1-minute load of 24.36 with nothing else running.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted and explained rather than relabelled. The CSV is the raw artifact and its numbers are what was measured; the report states that the phase named idle means no load beyond the gate's own, and gives the range. Rewriting a recorded artifact to match a better label is the worse trade.
